across_instances_of_the_SAME_environment.the_one: ring_rotate: three states, goal absent, so every instance is the same trivial machine -- the single instance-invariant case is also the case nothing can be solved in
across_instances_of_the_SAME_environment.why: instances differ by their START state (grid_walk (0,0) vs (1,1); cyclic_counter 0 vs 1; dial_lock (0,0,0) vs (1,0,0)). The transition function is the same SHAPE; the labelled machine from the start is not, because the goal-distance labels differ. So last round's 33/33 carry is REAL but it is carry of the TRANSITIONS, not of the machine identity -- the table is reused exactly where it was already correct and is re-keyed elsewhere

the_abstraction_does_not_fold.measure: bisimulation quotient under goal-distance labels, by kind
the_abstraction_does_not_fold.finding: blocks == |S| for 15 of 16 exactly-decidable kinds (grid_walk 16, dial_lock 64, tri_lock 60, adjacent_sort 24, double_dial 20, bit_register 16, toggle_bank 16, parity_lights 8, binary_odometer 16, last_wins 4, cyclic_counter 7, sliding_pairs 24)
the_abstraction_does_not_fold.meaning: these environments are STRONGLY ASYMMETRIC: almost every state has a distinct future, so the coarsest exact abstraction is the state space itself. A structural table therefore cannot be smaller than the state space, and cannot fold two environments together unless they fold internally first

why_no_transfer_is_even_possible_here.the_tree_says_so_itself: cross_kind_learning_to_learn_benchmark_v1.py, on its held-out kinds: 'Composed from the same structural vocabulary ... deliberately none is a copy of one.' The no-transfer result confirms the benchmark achieved what it set out to do

the_trade_off_reproduced_on_the_trees_ow.source: OPSR, arXiv 2604.07016: a finer abstraction is always more control-granular and less likely to transfer

measured.consequence: coarsening creates the collisions that permit transfer AND destroys the distinctions control needs; the trade-off is real and it is exactly as the literature states

next_step: Build a substrate whose environments genuinely share machines -- same dynamics under renamed actions, different start states, different goal labels -- and measure executed transfer on it, with the correspondence found and not supplied. Two environments made identical would measure nothing and must be avoided.
